import seaborn as sns
import io

# Load the dataset from the provided string
data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(data))

# Set a visually appealing seaborn style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the scatter plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7)) # Set a larger figure size for better readability

# Use a scatter plot to show relationships between continuous variables
# and encode categorical variables using hue, style, and size.

    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='sensor_type',       # Color points based on sensor type
    style='body_type',       # Use different marker styles for body type

    sizes=(100, 1000),       # Define the range of marker sizes
    palette='viridis',       # Choose a color palette
    edgecolor='black',       # Add a black edge to markers for better distinction
    linewidth=1              # Set the width of the marker edge
)

# Annotate each point with the brand name for clarity, especially with a small dataset
for index, row in df.iterrows():
     scatter_plot.text(row['megapixels'] + 0.5, # Offset text slightly to the right of the point
                       row['price_usd'],
                       row['brand'],
                       horizontalalignment='left',
                       verticalalignment='center',
                       size='medium',
                       color='black',
                       weight='semibold')

# Set plot title and labels

# Adjust plot layout to make room for the legend
